_comment: Which candidates go to upload/. Numbers are the NN in the filename, which
is the index of the shot() call in integration_test/store_screenshots.dart —
so 05 is the same screen in every language. Reordering that file's screen
list invalidates these numbers.
Keyed per locale rather than with a '*' on purpose: only en-US and ja have a
complete 50-frame pool. ko stopped at 30, and zh-CN / zh-TW were never shot.
A '*' here would try to select frame 32 out of ko's 30 and fail. When those
three runs are finished, replace the two keys below with:
The eight, and why each earns its slot:
02 home_today        the app at a glance — waveform, detected languages,
transcript, record button, all in one frame
05 search_spoken_words  search by what was SAID, with a tappable
timestamp that plays from that moment. The
differentiator; nothing else here is unusual.
13 model_download_sheet  the offline promise in the app's own words:
'Transcription runs fully offline. The speech model
(228 MB) is downloaded once and kept on this device.'
14 history_calendar  the month grid that indexes the archive
17 history_long_transcript  several transcribed recordings stacked — what
the archive turns into after a few weeks
21 settings          storage as hours, not bytes: '19 min recorded · about
18 h 18 min still fits'. Matters for a long-form
recorder and no competitor screenshot shows it.
28 recording         recording in progress: timer, pause, and the
hold-for-live-text panel
32 dark_home         dark mode, hand-built rather than an inversion
Swaps worth considering:
13 -> 04  if leading with a 228 MB download reads as a cost rather than a
promise. 04 shows the Transcribe button instead.
21 -> 22  the language sheet, if the listing should lead on the five UI
languages rather than on storage.
Suggested display ORDER in the Console (drag to reorder there; the Console
shows them in upload order, and this file's order is lexical by number):
